issues.title: Triangle areas omitted from the discrete-current estimator

failure_location.quote: The weights $\tau_{i,S},\tau_{i,T}$ are defined as $\tau_{\hat{S}}(c_{i,S}),\tau_{\hat{T}}(c_{i,T})$ respectively.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the normal vector at $x \in S$ scaled by the area of the approximating triangle

issues.failure_explanation: By currdef, a triangle contributes the integral of the tangent 2-vector against surface measure. Even for a test form constant on one triangle, midpoint quadrature gives its area times τ(c_i), not merely τ(c_i). The old weights are defined as the unit tangent vectors alone, so the resulting estimator and product are count-weighted rather than area-weighted and are not a consistent surface quadrature in general.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete current and its kernel product depend incorrectly on tessellation density and need not approximate the continuous current or its RKHS inner product.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each triangle, replace the unit tangent weight τ(c_i) by a_iτ(c_i), where a_i is the triangle area, in both discrete currents. Use these weighted atoms in discinnerprodcurr, equivalently inserting the product of the two triangle areas in each pairing, and state consistency for this area-weighted midpoint quadrature.
issues.why_classification: The count-weighted estimator is a genuine construction error rather than a mere index slip. Nevertheless, currdef and the old source's later area-scaled-normal description directly support a short, standard quadrature correction that preserves the intended current metric and consistency guarantee.

issues.title: Incorrect semicircle normalization in the cylindrical metric term
issues.failure_explanation: Let a=f/|f| and let β_T=-a×n_T be the inward unit direction. Parametrizing the specified semicircle by arc length gives ∫_C u dH^1(u)=2β_T. The old calculation instead uses (π/2)β_T. Consequently each cylindrical atom has magnitude factor 2 and the atom-pairing prefactor is 4, whereas the old theorem states π²/4. The separate sign error in the tangent basis is adjudicated under C04.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem mis-scales every cylindrical edge-edge contribution, and the same wrong normalization propagates to the cylindrical atomic weights and vector-valued embedding.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keeping the orientation convention fixed, parameterize the specified semicircle by arc length and replace its vector integral (π/2)β_T by 2β_T. Propagate this normalization through the cylindrical delta weights and vector-valued embedding, and replace the cylindrical atom-pairing coefficient π²/4 by 4.
issues.why_classification: The old derivation uses a mathematically false integral, so this is not a transcriptional typo. The required work is only an elementary one-dimensional integral followed by local constant bookkeeping; it needs no new proof architecture and preserves every substantive guarantee.

issues.title: Omitted hemisphere factor in surface-boundary and curve metrics
issues.failure_explanation: For K_s=1, the spherical contribution at a boundary or curve vertex is obtained by integrating over oriented hemispheres. The old derivation states ∫_{S^+_α}u dH²(u)=πα, so each vertex atom carries a factor π and a bilinear pairing carries π². Nevertheless, both the surface theorem's boundary term and the later discrete-curve theorem use π²/4. The stated formal conclusions therefore disagree with the normalization established by the paper's own calculation.
issues.overall_effect: Boundary contributions to the triangulated-surface metric and all contributions to the discrete-curve metric are scaled incorrectly; the old boundary coefficient in the vector embedding is inconsistent for the same reason.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the old source's stated identity that the vector integral over the oriented hemisphere is πα. Give each spherical boundary or curve-vertex atom the factor π and hence each corresponding bilinear pairing the factor π², replacing the affected π²/4 theorem coefficients and the π/2 boundary coefficient in the vector embedding.
issues.why_classification: The old source already states the correct hemisphere integral and derives a π-weighted spherical component. The contrary coefficients are uniquely identifiable copied normalization errors; correcting them requires no replacement inference and changes no substantive guarantee.

issues.title: Negatively oriented cylindrical basis presented as positive

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $(e_{1}(x,u),e_{2}(x,u),u)$ is a positively oriented orthonomal basis, it implies $u = e_{1}(x,u) \times e_{2}(x,u)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the displayed triple is a positively oriented orthonormal basis. In fact, if a=f/|f|, then the cross product of its first two vectors is a×(a×u)=-u, so the triple is negatively oriented. Replacing the second vector by -a×u makes the cross product equal to u and restores the claimed orientation.
issues.overall_effect: The tangent 2-vector and hence the orientation of the derived cylindrical functional are reversed. A common sign can cancel in a purely cylindrical inner product, but the asserted oriented normal-cycle decomposition itself is wrong.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Writing a=f/|f|, replace the displayed cylindrical basis (a,a×u,u) by (a,−a×u,u), for which a×(−a×u)=u. Propagate the resulting sign through the cylindrical tangent 2-vector and atomic normal-cycle decomposition while leaving scalar normalizations unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The erroneous basis is actually substituted into the cylindrical derivation, so the defect requires sign checking and propagation and is not merely typographical. That repair is nevertheless short and routine, and it restores the oriented functional without changing the method or any metric guarantee.

issues.title: Midpoint quadrature asserted as an exact normal-cycle decomposition
issues.failure_explanation: The assumption K_s=1 makes test forms independent of the spherical variable, not of the spatial variable x. Thus replacing the integral along an edge by its midpoint value generally leaves a nonzero quadrature remainder. The old source correctly writes the individual replacement as an approximation, but NC_delta then asserts an equality for N(\mathcal T) without retaining or declaring the sum of those remainders.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed atomic functional is a midpoint-discretized surrogate rather than the exact embedded normal cycle. The generic compression theorem remains valid for that surrogate, but comparison with the exact normal cycle additionally requires the quadrature error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the displayed finite Dirac sum as a midpoint surrogate N̂(𝒯). For each cylindrical edge contribution define its exact quadrature remainder R_j as the edge integral minus its midpoint replacement, and state N(𝒯)=N̂(𝒯)+Σ_jR_j. Apply the compression theorem to N̂(𝒯); whenever an error against the exact normal cycle is claimed, add the norm of the summed remainder and provide the applicable midpoint-quadrature consistency bound.
issues.why_classification: This is resolvable without global reconstruction, and the compression method survives for the same recognizable midpoint surrogate. However, the exact finite-Dirac decomposition and exact-target error guarantee do not survive unchanged: they acquire a genuine quadrature remainder. That limited but substantive weakening exceeds a minor same-guarantee edit.

issues.title: Cylindrical atoms moved off their edge-centre supports
issues.failure_explanation: The midpoint cylindrical atom is δ_{c_i}γ_i, with c_i the edge centre. The old source defines F on atoms by F(δ_xτ)=δ_xB(τ), which preserves the spatial support. It therefore cannot map δ_{c_i}γ_i to δ_{x_i}B(γ_i); moreover x_i is otherwise used for boundary vertices. The first sum in realembedding has the wrong source locations.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed vector-valued functional is not the isometric image of the cylindrical normal-cycle approximation, so compression of that displayed functional would use incorrect spatial kernel centres.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the first sum of realembedding, replace each cylindrical support δ_{x_i} by δ_{c_i}. Thus F maps δ_{c_i}γ_i to δ_{c_i}B(γ_i), while the boundary atoms remain supported at their boundary vertices x_i.
issues.why_classification: Both NC_delta and the explicit rule F(δ_xτ)=δ_xB(τ) uniquely force preservation of the edge-centre c_i. The occurrence of x_i is a local support-label transcription error requiring no mathematical reconstruction.

issues.title: Compression bounds use an undefined target functional
issues.failure_explanation: The target is μ_S=Σ_iδ_{x_i}α_i and the constructed approximation is Σ_jδ_{c_j}β_j. No coefficients hat α_i are introduced. Consequently the approximation statement and both trace and eigenvalue bounds refer to an undefined functional and, literally, do not bound the compression error of μ_S.
issues.overall_effect: As written, neither advertised estimate is a well-defined guarantee for the target processed by the compression algorithm, although the intended target and approximation are unambiguous from the surrounding definitions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace every undefined coefficient hat α_i in the approximation statement, trace bound, and eigenvalue bound by the already defined α_i. Equivalently, define μ̂_S=Σ_jδ_{c_j}β_j and write both bounds directly as norms of μ_S−μ̂_S.
issues.why_classification: The target μ_S and the computed approximation are unambiguous from the theorem and algorithm, and no alternative meaning of hat α_i is defined. Removing the stray hats is uniquely forced notation repair and leaves the estimates and their guarantees unchanged.
